===Etymology 1===
{{ety|en|id=place|:inh|enm:putten|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|putten}}, {{m|enm|pitten}}, {{m|enm|pytten}}, {{m|enm|puten}}, {{m|enm|poten}}, from {{inh|en|ang|putian}}, {{m|ang|*pūtian}} {{gloss|"to push, put out"; attested by derivative {{m|ang|putung|t=pushing, impulse, instigation, urging}}}} and {{m|ang|potian|t=to push, thrust, strike, butt, goad}}, both from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*putōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*putōną|t=to stick, stab}}, which is of {{unc|en|nocap=1}} origin. Possibly from {{der|en|ine-pro|*bud-|t=to shoot, sprout}}, which would make it cognate with {{cog|sa|बुन्द||tr=bundá|arrow}}, {{cog|lt|budė}}, and {{m|lt|budis|t=mushroom, fungus}}. Compare also related {{cog|ang|pȳtan|t=to push, poke, thrust, put out (the eyes)}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|poten|t=to set, plant}}, {{cog|nds|paten|t=to set, plant}}, {{cog|da|putte|t=to put}}, {{cog|sv|putta}}, {{m|sv|pötta}}, {{m|sv|potta|t=to strike, knock, push gently, shove, put away}}, {{cog|no|putte|t=to set, put}}, {{cog|no|pota|t=to poke}}, {{cog|is|pota|t=to poke}}, {{cog|nl|peuteren|t=to pick, poke around, dig, fiddle with}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb|~s|~ting|~|+,~ten<l:UK,_,dialectal>}}

# To physically [[place]] ([[something]] or [[somebody]], in, at, around, etc. [[someplace]]).
#: {{syn|en|locate}}
#: {{ux|en|She '''put''' her books on the table.}}
#: {{ux|en|The police '''put''' him in a cell.}}
#: {{ux|en|They '''put''' the new motorway right through the [[national park]].}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|chapter=8|passage=Philander went into the next room{{...}}and came back with a salt mackerel that dripped brine like a rainstorm. Then he '''put''' the coffee pot on the stove and rummaged out a loaf of dry bread and some hardtack.}}
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=20|passage=‘No. I only opened the door a foot and '''put''' my head in. The street lamps shine into that room. I could see him. He was all right. Sleeping like a great grampus. Poor, poor chap.’}}
# To [[place]] in abstract; to attach or attribute; to assign.
#: {{ux|en|The government '''put''' restrictions on vehicle imports.}}
#: {{ux|en|I '''put''' £100 on the winning horse.}}
#: {{ux|en|Don't '''put''' the blame on me.}}
#: {{ux|en|What answer did you '''put''' for question 3?}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''put''' a wrong construction on an act or expression}}
#: {{ux|en|That seems like a bad idea '''put''' against the restrictions we're working under.}}
# To [[bring]] or [[set]] (into a certain [[relation]], [[state]] or [[condition]]).
#: {{ux|en|'''Put''' your house in order!}}
#: {{ux|en|He is '''putting''' all his energy into this one task.}}
#: {{ux|en|She tends to '''put''' herself in dangerous situations.}}
#: {{ux|en|The doctor's '''put''' me on a strict diet.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Put''' the following sentences into the past tense.}}
#: {{ux|en|[[put to bed|'''put''' to bed]]; [[put to shame|'''put''' to shame]]; [[put to death|'''put''' to death]]; [[put into practice|'''put''' into practice]]; [[put one's mind to it|'''put''' one's mind to it]]}}
#* {{RQ:Milton History|11|Theſe Verſes Originally Greek, were '''put''' in Latin,}}
# To [[express]] (something in a certain manner).
#: {{ux|en|When you '''put''' it that way, I guess I can see your point.}}
#: {{ux|en|To '''put''' it bluntly, he's an idiot.}}
#: {{ux|en|To '''put''' it simply, we can't afford it.}}
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1846|author=w:Julius Hare|title=The Mission of the Comforter
|passage=All this is ingeniously and ably '''put'''.}}
# To [[set]] before one for [[judgment]], [[acceptance]], or [[rejection]]; to [[bring]] to the [[attention]].
#: {{ux|en|I '''put''' it to you, Sir, that you are a thief and a liar.}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''put''' a question; to '''put''' a case}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1708-1710|author=w:George Berkeley|title=Philosophical Commentaries or Common-Place Book
|text='''Put''' the perceptions and you '''put''' the mind.}}
#* {{RQ:Orwell Animal Farm|3
|passage=Now if there was one thing that the animals were completely certain of, it was that they did not want Jones back. When it was '''put''' to them in this light, they had no more to say.}}
#* {{quote-journal|1=en|journal=w:TIME|title=Iceland’s E.U. Referendum, Explained|date=August 18 2026|author=Tiago Ventura|text=The exact question being '''put''' to voters for a yes or no answer is: “Should Iceland reopen accession negotiations with the European Union?”|url=https://time.com/article/2026/08/11/iceland-european-union-referendum-what-it-means/|accessdate=18 August 2026|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260819004041/https://time.com/article/2026/08/11/iceland-european-union-referendum-what-it-means/|archivedate=19 August 2026}}
# To [[set]] as a [[calculation]] or [[estimate]].
#: {{ux|en|They have '''put''' the cost of repairs at around £10 million.}}
# To steer; to direct one's course; to go.
#: {{ux|en|[[put to sea|to '''put''' to sea]]}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|6|passage=His fury thus appeased, he '''puts''' to land.}}
# {{lb|en|finance}} To sell (assets) under the terms of a [[put option]].
#: {{ux|en|He got out of his Procter and Gamble bet by '''putting''' his shares at 80.}}
# {{lb|en|especially|athletics}} To [[throw]] with a pushing motion, especially in reference to the sport of ''[[shot put]]''. {{q|Do not confuse with ''[[putt]]''.}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''put''' the shot out beyond the 20-metre mark.}}
# To play a card or a hand in the game called "put".
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To lay down; to give up; to surrender.
#* {{RQ:Wycliffe Bible|IV|John|15|13|280|passage=No man hath more love than this, that a man '''put''' his life for his friends.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To incite; to entice; to urge; to constrain; to oblige.
#* {{quote-text|en|year=1722|author=w:Jonathan Swift|title=[[s:The Works of the Rev. Jonathan Swift/Volume 9/The Last Speech of Ebenezer Elliston|The Last Speech of Ebenezer Elliston]]
|passage=These wretches '''put''' us upon all mischief.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=4|line=386|passage=Thank him who '''puts''' me loath to this revenge|year=1873}}
#* {{RQ:Scott Peveril of the Peak|passage='''Put''' me not to use the carnal weapon in my own defence.}}
# {{lb|en|mining}} To convey [[coal]] in the mine, as for example from the [[working]] to the [[tramway]].<ref>{{R:Raymond Glossary}}</ref>

=====Usage notes=====
The verb "put" is unusual in that most senses require an adverbial for completion of the idea. For example, you cannot just "put a book", you must "put a book on the table", "put a book in the wastebin", etc.
